newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda premier a target in corruption case - paper.
newsitem.headline: Uganda premier a target in corruption case - paper.

text.p: An investigation into corruption in the Uganda Railway Corporation is being extended to Prime Minister Kintu Musoke and Information Minister Ruhukana Rugunda, the independent Monitor newspaper reported on Sunday.
The paper quoted Ugandan Vice-President Specioza Wandira Kazibwe as saying her office was investigating allegations that the two were involved in illegal deals in houses belonging to the URC.
No comment from the two was immediately available.
Last month Kirunda Kivejinja resigned as transport minister after being named by a parliamentary committee, and URC general manager Enos Tumusiime resigned last week.

Uganda's railways were part of the East African rail system until the East African Community linking Uganda with Kenya and Tanzania broke up in 1977. The URC ended passenger services on its 1,241 km (770 miles) of track last October because they were losing money.
